description: The length floor's shape exception. A paragraph shorter than the run's min_text_length has no request built for it, which is the right default: most of what is that short is a folio, a rule, or a piece of a word the paragraph finder broke off, and none of those is a sentence anyone wants translated. But some of it is a whole written unit that happens to be short -- a section label on a contents page, a byline standing on its own line -- and on a document translated out of its source language those come out untranslated in the middle of a translated page. So a second, lower floor applies to paragraphs of a declared shape, and to nothing else. shape_exception_floor is that lower floor. short_label_max_chars is the longest a label_shaped paragraph may be. name_min_words and name_max_words bound how many words a name_shaped paragraph may hold. Both shapes additionally have to be solitary: no other paragraph may stand within adjacent_gap_ratio of the paragraph's own font size of it, horizontally, on the same line band. That is the test that separates the two things a short paragraph can be. A section label sits alone on its band with the width of a column between it and anything else, and a piece of a broken word sits hard against the piece that follows it -- the gap between them is the gap between two letters. The ratio is a multiple of the font size rather than a length, so the same shape decides alike at any size, and a paragraph in another column of the same band is not adjacent to anything. Beyond both shapes a paragraph has to be one the source audit did not place as a broken word: the audit reads the page a second time through code the pipeline does not share, and a paragraph whose characters are part of a word that reading holds whole is a fragment however solitary its box makes it look. Those go to the fragment stitch, which is the repair they want, and never here. switch names the run attribute the whole pass is read from; with it down no paragraph below the floor reaches a request, which is every run before this pass existed. shapes is the closed vocabulary a admitted paragraph is recorded under, and every record carries one of them. min_letters is the fewest letters an admitted paragraph may hold. A figure is not a written unit and there is nothing in it to translate: the page batch already refuses a paragraph of digits alone, and a paragraph of digits with a sign beside it is the same thing wearing a sign. ideographic_exception_floor is the still lower floor a wholly-Han paragraph reaches down to: one ideograph is one word -- the single-character unit or axis label a chart prints -- where one Latin letter is not, so the general floor stays at two while a Han-only label of one character is admitted. Two further script-aware judgments ride the same measurement. A neighbour written wholly in a different script bucket does not defeat solitarity, because the solitary test exists to catch pieces of a broken word and a word does not break across scripts. And a candidate whose box intersects its own other-script double -- a masthead printed in two languages on one spot -- is refused with reason bilingual_companion rather than translated, because the target-language half is already on the page and a translation would say the same thing twice on the same ink. companion_ink_min_fraction and companion_render_zoom serve the bilingual companion exemption's visibility condition: the exemption that skips translating a label whose other-script double shares its ink area now also demands that the double demonstrably renders -- the source page's own pixels over the companion's box must depart from the region's background colour in at least companion_ink_min_fraction of the sampled pixels, rasterized at companion_render_zoom. A companion drawn in background colour, wholly covered by an opaque object, clipped away, outside the crop box, or unrenderable (no readable source file, a partial-page run) proves nothing, and the unit is translated: an untranslated label harms more than a doubled one.
